source: Statement Classifier — Specification v1.0, §3.2 (the fifteen definitions)
note: Cues are drawn from the taxonomy's own definitions, which that document requires be written as surface tests rather than judgment calls. A match protects a unit from being dropped in synthesis; it does NOT assign it a type -- classification runs separately, after digestion. Because of that, the cues are deliberately LOOSE: this net only decides what must not be lost, and the downstream classifier makes the real call. A false positive costs one unit carried forward that need not have been; a false negative costs a definition nobody can find.

protected.label: definition
protected.why: States what a term means. Asserts nothing to argue with, so a planner describes it instead of carrying it, and the reader loses the ability to apply the term.

protected.label: procedure
protected.why: An operational instruction. A reader must be able to follow it from the output alone; a summary of it is unusable.

protected.label: obligation
protected.why: A standing requirement someone is accountable to. Dropping it turns a rule into an omission nobody can detect.

protected.label: prohibition
protected.why: A hard rule that can be violated. Its absence from the output reads as permission.

protected.label: formula
protected.why: Says what a quantity equals. Paraphrasing an equation destroys it.

protected.label: dependency
protected.why: A hard requirement without which the thing cannot run. Losing it makes the output describe something that will not work.

protected.label: assumption
protected.why: A precondition the rest rests on. Dropped, every claim above it reads as unconditional.
